newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Gold-Prices hold as local trading eases.
newsitem.headline: Australia Gold-Prices hold as local trading eases.

text.p: Gold prices in Australia on Friday held onto the gains posted in New York and local bullion dealers predicted a consolidation at around US$321.00 an ounce.

The dealers said they were not expecting much retracement before the weekend in bullion, which rebounded to around US$319.60 late in New York on Thursday, a day after the precious metal was fixed in London at US$315.75, the lowest in 12 years.
"There seemed to be some consolidating here, there seems to be some support for the price building up," one said.
The Perth Mint quoted spot gold at US$321.03 and A$431.84 in late Friday afternoon trading.
"Based on what we're seeing now, you're unlikely to see much outside of US$317 and US$322 an ounce," the dealer added.
Meanwhile, the Australian government and its central bank have lashed out at critics and have defended the decision to sell 167 tonnes of gold in favour of securities backed in foreign currencies.

Deputy Australian Prime Minister Tim fischer blamed "24-year-old screen jockey's with braces for gold's falling prices on international markets, while Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said gold miners were exaggerating the price impact of the sale
These remarks followed comments last Friday by Australian Treasurer Peter Costello supporting the sales.
Gold trading activity in Sydney banks had slowed markedly by late afternoon on Friday following an abnormal high level of activity earlier in the week, another dealer said.
"Today was probably the quietest day of the week...But Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday were certainly three of the busiest days I've seen here," the dealer said.
He said the fact that gold prices bounced as high as US$321 an ounce (bid) in New York on Thursday suggests the actual trading range might be shrinking.
The expiry of COMEX August gold options on Friday is unlikely to hold much sway in the market given, most are out of the money.
But this is not to suggest gold prices are less susceptible to another downturn as the market continues to absorb last week's RBA gold sales.
"At the moment, I still still favour another look to the downside," another dealer said.
Others agreed, saying the recent lift in the price was little more than speculators testing of the upside potential ahead of taking some profits.
"It's becoming clear the funds have had a pretty good run in the last few day, and they've got to start taking profits at some point," a dealer in Melbourne said.
Local criticism from Australia's gold industry over the RBA sales has not translated into much new forward selling business, the dealers said.
In most cases, Australia's gold miners are adequately and properly hedged out two or three years, they said.
"The price would have to stay down here for a long time to see a big push in fresh hedging," one said.

"Certainly, there are some smaller companies that probably don't have their hedging in place like some of the larger houses do, but most view the current price above all as just a point in the cycle."
However, the Perth mint estimates that about 25 medium to large Australian mines have total costs at or above current world prices.
Dealers said this points to more miners contemplating taking out additional hedges.
This already is being reflected in implied gold borrowing rates running at about two percent, double what they typically are, dealers said.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
